title: Add cryptographic consent receipts, transient RBAC leases, and locality-aware KMS proxy
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduces cryptographic consent receipts (immutable per-request proof), transient RBAC lease mechanism for operator elevation, and a locality-aware KMS proxy with optional HSM wrapping for private installs. Improves auditability and data-residency compliance; opt-in for existing clusters.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers operating in regulated jurisdictions asked for non-repudiable proof of customer consent and tighter, timebound operator privileges for troubleshooting in Private deployments. This PR implements three coordinated features:
1) Cryptographic consent receipts: a compact, signed message produced at request time that proves which tenant/route consented to processing, the consent policy version, and the KMS key identity used to encrypt artifacts. Receipts are signed with a service-level signing key (optionally HSM-backed for private installs) and appended to the audit-append log.
2) Transient RBAC leases: small changes to the RBAC v2 stack to support short-lived, auditable operator grants (leases) with approver metadata, TTL, and automatic revocation. Leases are issued via the operator-approval service and are required for any privileged action (keys, secret views, cross-zone replay).
3) Locality-aware KMS proxy: a proxy layer that pins KMS calls to tenant-preferred regions when available; it supports a mirror-write fallback (writes to primary then asynchronously mirrors metadata to secondary KMS endpoints for cross-region failover), and exposes explicit key-identity claims used inside consent receipts. Private-installer integration: adds configuration knobs for using customer HSMs (PKCS#11) and local KMS endpoints; installer artifacts include CRD schema updates and systemd unit for kms-proxy when running on-prem.
Checklist:
- [x] CR: Consent receipt protobuf + signer and verification helpers
- [x] RBAC: lease lifecycle, approval workflow endpoints, enforcement gates
- [x] KMS proxy: routing, mirror-write, key-identity header plumbing
- [x] Audit: append-only receipt consumer and indexer; retention hook configurable
- [x] Private-installer: PKCS#11 configuration and sample playbook
- [x] Docs: design doc and operator runbook
- [x] E2E tests and unit coverage
Notes about backwards compatibility and opt-in: Consent receipts and transient leases are disabled by default on hosted API to avoid changing existing request headers. Private deployments can enable them via operatorConfig. The KMS proxy supports a compatibility mode where it only annotates requests (no mirroring) to ease rollout.
Security considerations: signer key rollover is supported via a keyproof handshake; receipt verification is validated in CI harness. Lease issuance requires two approver roles for high-sensitivity actions (configurable threshold).
Migration plan:
- Step 1 (canary): enable receipt generation in dedicated QA region with mirror disabled
- Step 2: enable transient leases in admin-only clusters, keep enforcement soft-fail for 2 weeks
- Step 3: enable full enforcement and mirror-write for KMS where latency tests pass

notes_for_ops: Enable feature flags: operator.features.consents=false by default. To enable in private-installer set operatorConfig.features.consents=true and provide signer PKCS#11 config. Monitor audit.indexer.receipt_ingest_lag and kms.proxy.mirror_queue_depth.
security_risk_summary: Signed receipts provide non-repudiable evidence of consent; signer key management requires HSM or careful rotation policies. Transient leases limit blast radius but increase complexity in operator workflows. Mirror writes risk duplicate metadata; mirror worker enforces idempotency and write-rate limits.
